correctness.rationale: For every triple, the vanishing of the three character values is iff its sum vector annihilates the frequency difference and its first edge does not. Requiring this on all three frequency differences gives the two common-sum fiber constraints and two bijective edge-evaluation constraints. Quotient rank 1 yields one choice in each of three fibers, \(3^{3d-2r-3}\); rank 2 yields six permutations of the second coordinate and three choices of representatives, \(6\,3^{3d-2r-6}\); if an edge lies in the sum span there are none. Changing spatial ordering does not affect these ranks. Elementary affine-plane orbit counting exactly proves the 7056-pair histogram. The independent modular brute program verifies all d=2 pairs and all frequency triples for selected larger-dimension pairs, without using floating point; computation is corroboration, not proof in infinite dimensions.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic searches were cross-checked against actual inspected primary full text. A 2019 paper discusses simultaneous *Riesz* (invertible) bases, not orthogonal common spectral bases; a 2021 paper gives individual spectral zero/equidistribution criteria rather than arbitrary-pair exact counts. An indexed binary three-point common *Riesz* basis theorem concerns invertibility, and an affine-plane complete minor-rank classification concerns nonsingularity; neither entails orthogonality, exact spectrum multiplicity, or arbitrary pairs in all ternary dimensions. Cyclic single-support three-spectrum counts also lack these quantifiers. The complete ternary pair obstruction and exact number were not found; older independently indexed formulations remain possible.
residual_risks: An older ternary geometric design enumeration, possibly not indexed by Fourier-spectral terminology, could contain the equivalent two-triple count.
The three papers inspected in full are significant comparators, not an exhaustive census of the historical literature.
Indexed research-result summaries were compared by stated implications; inaccessible full texts of peripheral possibly relevant work were not certified to omit the result.

The affine-plane rank census and broader rank-deficient minor theory might be combined with additional orthogonality arguments to rederive the d=2 specialization, but do not themselves state or imply the all-dimensional common-spectrum multiplicity theorem.

value.rationale: Two simultaneous three-point Fourier apertures naturally seek the same perfectly conditioned orthogonal frequency basis. The quotient-rank obstruction is an exact, structural feasibility criterion and the formulas count every permissible unordered spectrum in every ternary vector dimension; a pair of individually spectral apertures can have no common optimal sampling set. The complete first noncyclic census has four nontrivial levels and 4320 incompatible ordered pairs. This information is absent from ordinary single-set spectrality or complete minor-rank censuses and matters precisely to shared multi-aperture Fourier sampling.
